src/domain/value-objects/Quantity.ts: Quantity.of is the only place that checks Number.isInteger(value), value < 1 and value > Quantity.MAX.
src/domain/value-objects/OrderStatus.ts: ORDER_STATUSES, FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE, CANCELLABLE_STATUSES, canTransition and stockEffectOf define the status lifecycle rules in one place.
src/domain/value-objects/OrderLine.ts: subtotalCents reads this.quantity.value, and toSnapshot unwraps the value object the same way, so OrderLine uses Quantity consistently.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The three files fit together as one concern: immutable domain value objects for orders. Each rule is kept in one place.

- Quantity.ts holds the quantity invariant: an integer from 1 to Quantity.MAX.
- OrderLine.ts uses Quantity.of rather than checking the quantity again. Its other fields are checked with the shared guards.
- OrderStatus.ts is the only place that defines the status list, the allowed status changes and the stock effect of each status.

No file skips the module's own abstractions. OrderStatus uses a const tuple and functions where the others use classes. That is a normal TypeScript pattern for an enum-like value, not an inconsistency. Quantity throws InvalidValueError directly while OrderLine calls shared guards. This is a small style difference and does not duplicate any rule.
